About VidFare

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

VidFare tracks what AI video generation actually costs, per second of finished video, across every place you can run a model. What every AI video second costs, everywhere.

Made by Emmanuel Gonzalez.

How the numbers work

  • Every price comes from the vendor's own pricing or model page, saved with a source link and the date we checked it.
  • Published rate: the vendor states dollars per second, or states an API credit count and a credit price. Runway API rows are credits per second times $0.01, the credit price on the Runway API pricing page.
  • From credit plan: plan price ÷ credits = $ per credit; × credits per clip ÷ clip length = $ per second. That assumes you use all your credits. It is not a list price per second.
  • Estimated from credit plan: the same math when the vendor says "~", "roughly", or "estimated" for the clip count. That label is not a list price. If a price cannot be confirmed, it is left out.
  • Audio, input, and length are copied from the vendor page. Audio is with audio, without audio, or not stated. Input is text-to-video, image-to-video, reference, video-to-video, extend, or lip-sync when that mode is named for the price. Length is the clip the credit price is for, a stated min and max, or a per-second rate the page ties to a length. If the page does not say it, the field stays not stated. A value is not inferred from a nearby sentence or from another row. A different stated price becomes its own row.
  • When a vendor shuts an endpoint down, that row is marked discontinued and kept under Discontinued with the last recorded rate. It is not used for cheapest picks.
  • Prices exclude VAT/sales tax and change often. Always confirm on the vendor's page before paying.
  • Deals are a separate list. A discounted $/s uses the vendor's stated rate or the checkout plan price ÷ credits. A code that lasts the first N months also shows a 12-month blended rate. Unlimited windows show how many seconds of video cover the plan price. They are not listed at $0/s. A deal on one variant is labelled with that variant, so it is not read as a discount on a different row.

How we source and check prices

Each row keeps the vendor page it came from and the date that page last matched its check. The daily job is scripts/update_prices.py --apply. GitHub Actions runs it at 15:17 UTC every day, and again at 13:30 UTC on Fridays, then rebuilds the site from the data files.

  • A source marked static is downloaded and read as page text. Some of those pages also keep a price in a script payload, and the check reads that payload when the row is set up for it.
  • A source marked render is opened in Chrome and read after the page loads. Higgsfield plans are one of these.
  • A source marked manual is not fetched. Kling app subscriptions are that source. The pricing page did not show prices without a login or a region, so those subscriptions are not in the table.
  • Each row and each plan has a needle: the phrase and the number stored for it. The check searches the fetched text for that phrase and compares the number with the stored value.
  • When an API row's number has changed, the job updates that row's dollars per second by the same factor and writes the old and new figures to the price-change log. A credit-plan row is not rewritten by that step. A plan whose price or credit count changed is flagged, and its dollars per second stay as stored.
  • A row whose needles still match is stamped with that day's date. A credit-plan row is not stamped when its plan failed the check.
  • A promo whose end date has passed is removed from the live table and recorded as ended. A live deal past its end date is marked ended.
  • The same run looks for new or removed sale-like sentences on the watched pricing pages. Those sentences are saved as unconfirmed candidates. They are not added to the deals list, and they do not change a price.
  • When every source except the manual one was fetched, last_full_check becomes that date.

The check compares stored numbers with the fetched page. It does not add a price the page did not state.

Not in the price table

  • Kling app (kling.ai) consumer subscription prices: The pricing page did not show a price without a login or a region, so there is no dollars-per-second row.
  • Replicate Wan 3.0 '30% off this week' banner: The model page did not show that discount on the price, so it is not in the table.
  • Replicate Wan 3.0 Prime (alibaba/wan-3-prime): The model page did not show a static price, so there is no row.
  • Higgsfield Seedance 2.5 per-clip credits: The plan page says '~80 Seedance 2.5 videos' for 1,200 credits and does not give clip length or resolution, so there is no dollars-per-second row.
  • Higgsfield Kling 3.0 credits: The compare table says ~7 credits/5s at 720p and the plan quiz says ≈14 credits per 8s 720p. Those two figures disagree, so neither is a dollars-per-second row.
  • Krea Max plan per-clip counts: The count column uses a 40k pack whose price is not shown, so Max has no row.
  • Kling 4.0: The official API page lists per-second rates, and input video changes the billed duration, so there is no single dollars-per-second row.

Some links on VidFare are affiliate links. If you sign up through them we may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you. Affiliate status never changes the order of the tables: rows are always sorted by price. Sponsored placements are labelled "Sponsor" and never affect the price order.
